config.theme: Family video call planning a cousin's wedding
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Family video call planning a cousin's wedding

personas.name: Abena
personas.hidden_agenda: Invited more of her church than she has admitted

personas.name: Yaw
personas.role: Bride's uncle, handling the Ghana side
personas.goals: Get every relative a visa in time
personas.hidden_agenda: Lending money to two cousins for their flights

personas.name: Efua
personas.goals: Keep both families happy and the budget sane

personas.name: Declan
personas.goals: Make the Irish side feel welcome
personas.hidden_agenda: Has never been to a Ghanaian engagement and is nervous

pack.title: Efua and Liam's wedding - family call

agenda.title: The two ceremonies
agenda.goal: Settle the engagement ceremony and the church wedding plans

agenda.title: Guests and travel
agenda.goal: Track the visas and the flights from Accra

agenda.title: Food
agenda.goal: Agree the menu across both families

agenda.title: Budget
agenda.goal: Check the big costs against the budget

beats.summary: The engagement and the church; Declan's questions
Visas and flights; Yaw's visa count is high; Declan's flight number stands
Two families, one menu; a little detour about a hurling match
The big costs; Abena's guest number contradicts the plan, corrected later

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: Hi, everyone. Can we start with the two ceremonies? Declan has questions.

turns.speaker: Declan
turns.text: I do. The engagement is the twelfth, the church is the nineteenth?

turns.speaker: Abena
turns.text: Yes. July twelfth for the engagement at the house, July nineteenth for the church.

turns.speaker: Declan
turns.text: And what do I wear to the engagement? I don't want to get it wrong.

turns.speaker: Abena
turns.text: Kente, if you can. We ordered fourteen yards, so there is cloth for Liam's side too.

turns.speaker: Declan
turns.text: Oh, that's very kind. Mam will cry.

turns.speaker: Yaw
turns.text: The engagement has a lot of steps. Someone from Liam's side has to speak for the family.

turns.speaker: Declan
turns.text: Speak? Me?

turns.speaker: Yaw
turns.text: Or your father. Someone who can say yes, the family agrees.

turns.speaker: Declan
turns.text: Dad will do it. He loves a speech. I'll tell him tonight.

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: Thank you. The engagement is at the house, the wedding is at the church, and nobody changes that now.

turns.speaker: Declan
turns.text: Got it.

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: Guests and travel. Uncle Yaw?

turns.speaker: Yaw
turns.text: We had eleven visa applications from Ghana, and nine are approved.

turns.speaker: Abena
turns.text: Nine! That's wonderful.

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: The tracker says six approved, Uncle. Three are still waiting for interviews.

turns.speaker: Yaw
turns.text: Six. Yes, the other three have their interviews next week.

turns.speaker: Declan
turns.text: How much are the flights from Accra?

turns.speaker: Yaw
turns.text: They're expensive in July.

turns.speaker: Declan
turns.text: I looked it up for curiosity. About nine hundred return, I think.

turns.speaker: Abena
turns.text: And the RSVPs? The deadline is the end of May.

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: Most people have replied. We're expecting about a hundred and eighty.

turns.speaker: Abena
turns.text: My church alone is a hundred.

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: Mum. The hall holds two hundred.

turns.speaker: Abena
turns.text: I'm only saying.

turns.speaker: Yaw
turns.text: Could someone help the three cousins with their interview paperwork?

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: I'll call each of them on Sunday and go through the forms.

turns.speaker: Yaw
turns.text: Thank you, Efua.

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: Food. The caterer can do both jollof and a roast.

turns.speaker: Declan
turns.text: Jollof and a roast. That's the best of both worlds.

turns.speaker: Abena
turns.text: And waakye at the engagement. That's not negotiable.

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: Fine, Mum. Waakye at the engagement.

turns.speaker: Declan
turns.text: Dad's going to be gutted, Kilkenny lost the hurling final on Sunday. He'll need cheering up.

turns.speaker: Yaw
turns.text: Hurling is the one with the sticks?

turns.speaker: Declan
turns.text: The fastest game on grass. It's like hockey crossed with a war.

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: The menu, people.

turns.speaker: Abena
turns.text: Will there be enough vegetarian food? Liam's mother doesn't eat meat.

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: The caterer has a vegetable stew and a mushroom roast.

turns.speaker: Abena
turns.text: Then that's the menu. Jollof, the roast, waakye at the engagement, and the vegetarian dishes.

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: Budget. The total is thirty-five thousand.

turns.speaker: Yaw
turns.text: The caterer quote is ninety-four hundred. That's the biggest single line.

turns.speaker: Abena
turns.text: For two hundred and fifty people, that's a good price.

turns.speaker: Declan
turns.text: Is it two fifty? I thought Efua said a hundred and eighty.

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: A hundred and eighty, Mum. The caterer quoted for a hundred and eighty.

turns.speaker: Abena
turns.text: A hundred and eighty. Then my church will have to share chairs.

turns.speaker: Yaw
turns.text: The photographer wants the eight hundred deposit by Friday.

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: I'll pay the photographer deposit tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Declan
turns.text: It might be worth asking the caterer whether the price holds if numbers change.

turns.speaker: Abena
turns.text: Maybe we just add ten more chairs for the church people and say nothing.

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: Mum. No.

turns.speaker: Yaw
turns.text: Has anyone told Liam's grandmother about the engagement customs? She might be surprised.

turns.speaker: Efua
turns.text: Okay. I think we've covered it. Thank you, all. Love you.

turns.speaker: Declan
turns.text: Love you too. Even the jollof.
